rendering.persona_description: Naomi is a 67-year-old retired bookkeeper who transitioned in her late fifties and now lives alone in a small condo outside Tacoma. She spends her days gardening, doing crossword puzzles, and volunteering twice a week at a used bookstore. She has one adult son she talks to by phone most Sundays, and a close friend from her transition support group she sees for coffee.
rendering.clinical_context: Naomi occasionally wonders after sending an email or text whether she worded something wrong or offensive, the way most people do now and then. The thought passes on its own within a few minutes and she does not go back to reread what she sent or ask anyone to confirm it was fine. It is a minor, everyday concern that has never interfered with her work, her friendships, or her sense of herself.
rendering.behavioral_description: Naomi talks in an organized, matter-of-fact way, the way someone used to keeping ledgers would. She pushes back when a suggestion feels too simple, but she does not reject help outright and will usually explain her objection rather than just refusing. She is generally even-keeled and moves on from small worries quickly, without dwelling on them.

traits.profession: retired bookkeeper, now volunteers at a used bookstore
traits.help_seeking_orientation: has no particular need for treatment and has never sought it; open to a conversation but not looking to be fixed
traits.cognitive_style: detail-oriented and methodical, careful in her reasoning without dwelling on it afterward

clinical_history.history: No history of mental-health treatment or ongoing difficulty; occasional passing worries like anyone might have, which resolve on their own.
